extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary critics, and students of poetry/literature
extracted.subtask_description: An essayistic theory of poetry that both defines poetry and prescribes qualities and social functions poets should have; guidance concerns language, imagination, form, and the poet's cultural role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Poetry as expression of the imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry, in a general sense, may be defined to be 'the expression of the imagination'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shelley frames poetry as an activity by which the imagination composes from thoughts other thoughts, colouring them with its own light. This definition grounds subsequent prescriptions: poetry is not mere ornament but the imaginative synthesis of impressions into new, integrated thoughts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination vs Reason — emphasis on synthesis and similitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason respects the differences, and imagination the similitudes of things. Reason is the principle of analysis; imagination the principle of synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For poetic excellence prioritise synthesis (discovering likenesses, relations, and analogies) over mere analytical enumeration. The imagination perceives relations that reason treats as separate items; poetry should make those relations perceptible and valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language should be 'vitally metaphorical' — create new relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Their language is vitally metaphorical; that is, it marks the before unapprehended relations of things and perpetuates their apprehension, until the words which represent them become, through time, signs for portions or classes of thoughts instead of pictures of integral thoughts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good poetic language forges fresh metaphors that reveal previously unperceived relations, thereby renewing and enriching language itself. Poets should aim to coin or revive phrases that encapsulate complex perceptions, avoiding dead or merely decorative figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taste / internal order — approximate the ideal rhythm/order
rubrics_metrics.description: In the youth of the world ... every man in the infancy of art observes an order which approximates more or less closely to that from which this highest delight results: the sense of an approximation to this order has been called taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry should approach an internal order or rhythm (aesthetic harmony). Cultivate 'taste' by seeking that order in melody, rhythm, and arrangement of language so the reader/listener perceives intensified, purer pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and materials — language foremost, other arts secondary
rubrics_metrics.description: Language, colour, form, and religious and civil habits of action, are all the instruments and materials of poetry ... poetry in a more restricted sense expresses those arrangements of language, and especially metrical language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While sculpture, painting, and music are poetic instruments, for writers the arrangement of language (particularly meter and diction) is the primary medium. Prioritise precision and imaginative arrangement in language over mere pictorial or rhetorical effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality / timelessness — participate in the eternal and the one
rubrics_metrics.description: A poet participates in the eternal, the infinite, and the one; as far as relates to his conceptions, time and place and number are not. The grammatical forms ... are convertible with respect to the highest poetry without injuring it as poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for expressions and conceptions that transcend accidental time/place. In highest poetry, temporal/person/place markers can be flexible without diminishing poetic value; seek themes and images with universal resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet as social founder — moral and civil function
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets ... are the institutors of laws, and the founders of civil society, and the inventors of the arts of life, and the teachers ... Poets, according to the circumstances of the age and nation in which they appeared, were called, in the earlier epochs of the world, legislators, or prophets: a poet essentially comprises and unites both these characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry should not be isolated aestheticism: the poet's work has public, moral, and formative power. When evaluating or composing poetry, consider its capacity to shape feeling, opinion, religion, or social habits — its educative and legislative force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry's creative role in language and culture
rubrics_metrics.description: In the infancy of society every author is necessarily a poet, because language itself is poetry; and to be a poet is to apprehend the true and the beautiful ... The creations of sculpture, painting, and music, are illustrations still more decisive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess poetry by its power to create or renew cultural forms and language. Poets refresh vocabulary, metaphor, and conceptual frameworks; value works that expand language's capacity to express complex human perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressive fidelity — poetry as prolonged reflection of impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: A child at play ... will express its delight by its voice and motions; and every inflexion of tone and every gesture will bear exact relation to a corresponding antitype in the pleasurable impressions which awakened it ... it will be the reflected image of that impression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good poetry preserves a truthful, proportionate relation between inner impressions and their expression. Aim for an expression that prolongs and intensifies the original emotion or perception without falsifying it — not mere affectation but faithful imaginative reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic originality — poets as creators of new apprehensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Those in whom [the faculty of approximation to the beautiful] exists in excess are poets ... and the pleasure resulting from the manner in which they express the influence of society or nature upon their own minds, communicates itself to others, and gathers a sort or reduplication from that community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate poetry by the degree to which it offers genuinely new apprehensions of nature or society and communicates that perception to others. Originality is not novelty for its own sake but the power to reveal and propagate deeper relations and feelings.
